newsitem.title: USA: Planned maintenance shuts more U.S. nuclear units.
newsitem.headline: Planned maintenance shuts more U.S. nuclear units.

text.p: Several U.S. nuclear power units, with an overall generating capacity of 2,959 megawatts (MW), shut this weekend for scheduled maintenance and refueling, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Monday.
The units join a long list of power stations already shut, taking advantage of typically light autumn electricity demand to carry out needed maintenance.
"We expect it to return to service near December 14," Olson said. Wisconsin Electric is a unit of Wisconsin Energy Corp.
Omaha Public Power District's 478 (MW) Fort Calhoun nuclear power unit 1 in Fort Calhoun, Neb. was also taken down Saturday for an estimated 44 days of refueling and maintenance, the NRC said.
Also, Duke Power Co shut its 846 MW Oconee nuclear power unit 3 on Friday afternoon, beginning early a maintenance and refueling outage that originally was expected to start November 3.
The unit was shut early for inspections of pipeline systems, following a Sept 24 accident at Oconee unit 2 in which a steam pipe burst and injured seven people.
Oconee 3 was expected to resume electricity production in mid-December.
Oconee units 1 and 2, each at Sececa, S.C. and with a capacity of 846 MW, were also shut for the pipe inspections and were expected to resume service in mid-November.
Nuclear operating companies usually schedule maintenance and refueling outages for the "shoulder" or low-demand months of spring and fall.
A total of about 21,160 MW of nuclear generation capacity in the U.S. was out of service for scheduled refueling and maintenance as of October 7.
In comparison, as of October 4, 1995 a total of 18,270 MW of power was out for scheduled refueling and maintenance.
The U.S. had a total 1996 estimated nuclear generation capacity of 100,504 MW.

Texas Utilities Co shut its 1,150 megawatt (MW) Comanche Peak nuclear power unit 1 Saturday for an estimated 42 days of scheduled refueling and maintenance, the NRC said in its daily plant status report.
The Comanche Peak 1 unit is located at Glen Rose, Texas.
Wisconsin Electric Power Co shut its 485 MW Point Beach nuclear power unit 2 on Saturday for an estimated 71 days, the NRC said.
The Two Rivers, Wis. unit will be refueled and a steam generator unit will be replaced, spokeswoman Jackie Olson said Monday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
